A high-contrast, hyper-stylized fashion editorial portrait shot against a saturated mustard-yellow seamless backdrop, with the central figure rendered in crisp desaturated black-and-white, creating a striking duotone aesthetic reminiscent of David LaChapelle meets Helmut Newton with a punk-gothic edge.

The subject is a fierce young woman with a platinum-bleached, spiked liberty mohawk crown of hair, her expression cold and commanding as she stares directly into the lens. She wears a cropped black leather biker jacket exploding with oversized metallic conical studs and spikes across the shoulders, paired with a minimal black bikini bottom, sheer black thigh-high stockings, and chunky knee-high lace-up combat platform boots. Her toned, athletic physique is fully exposed at the midriff.

She sits regally upon an ornate throne carved in the shape of a snarling, fanged beast's head — part dragon, part demonic feline — its silver-grey surface intricately detailed with bones, scales, and gothic ornamentation. Her booted foot rests on a battered metal road case wrapped in heavy chains and covered in stickers and band decals.

In her right hand she grips a massive medieval war scythe, its long wooden shaft wrapped in leather, the enormous curved blade arcing dramatically over her head. Perched on her left fist, talons gripping her knuckles, is a majestic American bald eagle with pristine white head feathers and a sharp yellow beak, staring off to the side with predatory alertness.

Studio lighting is hard and theatrical, casting crisp shadows. The composition is symmetrical, iconic, and poster-like — punk rock goddess of war meets American mythology. Hyperrealistic, high-fashion photography, 8k, sharp detail, magazine cover quality.

nodes.title: Note: MRLN Prompting
widgets_values:
# MRLN Prompting — Krea-2 Turbo

This graph is the pack's end-to-end example: the **Prompt Template (MRLN)**
node composes a prompt from the factory library, an optional LLM pass rewrites
it, and **Krea-2 Turbo** renders it in 8 steps.

## What the MRLN nodes do here

**Prompt Template (MRLN)** is the source of the prompt. It is set to
`animal/documentary` — pick any of the 100 shipped templates from the
`template` widget, or open the **Prompt Composer** sidebar tab (the book icon)
to browse them with thumbnails, pin individual slots and preview the result
before you queue anything. Its outputs are wired in the order you use them:

- `prompt` -> the positive prompt (via the enhance switch below)
- `llm` -> **Prompt Enhance (MRLN)**: one wire carrying the prompt, the
  profile's system prompt and any LoRA trigger words that must survive verbatim
- `loras` -> **LoRA Apply (MRLN)** in graphs that draw LoRA-bearing items
- `negative`, `choices`, `gen_info` -> the Show Text nodes, so you can see what
  was drawn, why, and what metadata the render carries

`seed` drives every random slot deterministically: the same seed and library
always draw the same prompt. Set `batch_count` above 1 and one queue renders a
whole batch of *different* draws instead of copies of one.

**Use enhanced Prompt** switches between the composed prompt and the LLM
rewrite. The Enhance node is set to a local Ollama model and to `pass through`
on error, so the graph still renders if no backend is running.

## Text to Image (Krea-2 Turbo) subgraph

Double-click it to open the pipeline. Inside: **Models** loads the diffusion
model, text encoder, VAE and an optional style LoRA; **Image Generation**
handles latent sizing, 8-step sampling and VAE decode. The `enable_lora?`
toggle on the left switches the style LoRA on.

## LoRAs, the MRLN way

This graph enables no style LoRA — the look comes from the prompt. When you do
want LoRAs, MRLN carries them *inside the prompt library* rather than as loader
nodes you wire by hand:

- Any item in a section or template can declare a LoRA block
- When that item is drawn, its LoRA leaves the node on the `loras` output
- **LoRA Apply (MRLN)** loads each one at the strength the item's author set,
  keeps the item's trigger words in the prompt verbatim, and warns when a
  LoRA's base family does not match the checkpoint
- A draw that selected no LoRA applies nothing, so the graph always runs

Add a LoRA to an item in the Composer's section editor and every template that
draws that item gains it — the prompt and the weights traveling together is the
whole point.
